Whether you're a math nerd or not, exploring the hyperbolic world of HyperRogue is a fascinating experience. The core gameplay mechanics are quite simple and easy to learn, but the game takes full advantage of its geometry to offer an entirely unique challenge in each of its MANY lands, via creative combination of enemies, traps, and (often most interestingly) level generation. The classic game mode is the main attraction, but there are also MANY other game modes and geometries to play around with, including a mode with "normal" Euclidean geometry, which really puts into perspective how HyperRogue is truly [i]more infinite[/i] than any Euclidean game!

Worth noting, this game is free and open source. I played the free version for well over 100 hours, but I recommend the Steam version, not only to support the developer, but also for the achievement system.

I could write an essay about how unique and interesting this game is, but this has been done to death already, so feel free to check many other in-depth reviews from other players around the web.

I still want to give my thumbs-up for this game, so I’ll make it simple and tell you what I would like to know beforehand why [b]HyperRogue[/b] is fascinating: it’s literally a turn-based score chaser with several layers of discoverability. There’s also Steam Leaderboards support, which is the cherry on top if you’re into improving your PBs and comparing highscores with other players.

[u]Friendly advice for newcomers:[/u] if you’re prone to motion sickness (like me), I suggest you to avoid fullscreen and go straight to windowed mode (on a medium or small window), which makes the whole experience much more comfortable and nausea-free.

Where Hyperbolica acts as an introduction to hyperbolic space, HyperRogue feels like it would be a clever successor to a long line of hyperbolic games. This is a marvelous achievement, given HyperRogue is, as far as I can tell, the first hyperbolic video game ever made! It actively takes advantage of curved space to make for excellent, strategic gameplay. In addition, because of the nature of hyperbolic space, exploring the world and finding new lands feels wonderful to me in a way no other game ever achieved, largely due to the infinite possibilities of where you might end up in every direction! There are 3D modes as well, giving you a full first person experience of the world. And if you want to explore the greater possibilities of curved space, HyperRogue grants access to 6 other geometries on top of that! My only problem is that some areas feel unreasonably difficult without much reward, which can discourage exploration. But with the incredible amount of effort put into this indie game to create something truly revolutionary, a mechanical flaw here or there certainly does not take away from the brilliance of it. In my opinion, the human race is lucky to have HyperRogue, and I recommend you let yourself experience it!

HyperRogue通关，通关时游戏时间为21.1h，算是第一个通关的Roguelike了。

游戏是在双曲空间下进行的网格、回合制游戏，以庞加莱圆盘的形式呈现（设置里可以换别的，例如上半平面等）。具体来说，就是给单位圆盘内部赋予一个不同的度量2ds/(1-r²)，换言之，到圆心距离为r的点附近的所有距离，都是通常意义下的距离的2/(1-r²)倍。

举个例子，庞加莱圆盘上以O为圆心，半径为r的圆C，设C上一点在通常意义下到圆心的距离为x，那么显然有
∫[0,x]2dt/(1-t²)=r，也就是ln((1+x)/(1-x))=r，所以x=tanh(r/2).
那么，C的周长=2πx*(2/(1-x²))=2π*(2tanh(r/2))/(1-tanh²(r/2))=2π*(2sinh(r/2)cosh(r/2))=2π*sinh(r).

这就说明了，双曲空间下，以O为圆心，半径为r的圆，其周长为2π*sinh(r).

相比之下，单位球面上取测地距离以后（等价于整个平面上取度量2ds/(1+r²)），半径为r的圆的周长是2π*sin(r).

而通常的平面，周长为2πr。这三个公式长得很像，而且不仅仅是长得像，其实就是2π*sin((√K)*r)/(√K)，K是高斯曲率。刚才的例子里K分别就是-1,1,0.


双曲空间的特性和平面完全不同。例如，因为K=-1，所以我们可以进行一个(6,6,7)镶嵌。有正七边形存在时，在遭遇包抄的时候更容易突围。例如，在被2个相邻的怪跟随时，可以跑到正七边形上，然后往反方向走就能逃脱。而在平面上的(6,6,6)镶嵌（全用正六边形）下，被2个相邻的怪跟随时就永远甩不掉了。游戏中还提供了单位球面上的(6,6,5)镶嵌，这个就更不可能了。

另外一个重要的特点就是，容易迷路。因为移动n格以后，可能到达的位置数是指数上升的。这就给游戏带来了和平面完全不同的特性。如果设至少走n步才能到的格子数有a(n)个，那么可以证明当n充分大时，有a(n+5)-2a(n+3)-2a(n+2)+a(n)=0。这就意味着a(n)=O(1.72208380573904^n)，准确地说底数是(1+√13+√(2(√13-1)))/4。如果换作平面上的(6,6,6)镶嵌，那么a(n)=6n，情况就完全不同了。其实连续的情形前面就算过，就是C=2π*sinh(r)和C=2πr的区别。



那么，说回游戏。游戏中，你和相当一部分小怪都是一击即毙的。回合制下，你先动一步（可以原地不动），其它敌人动一步。当你和敌人相邻时，轮到你后你可以干掉敌人（如果轮到敌人，敌人也可以干掉你）。游戏不允许你进行一个可能致死的移动。当你无法移动时，你就GAME OVER了。


游戏包括50多个区域。每个区域都有它特有的机制、特有的收集品、特有的小怪、特有的宝珠（提供不同的技能）。每个区域收集1、10、25、50个收集品都有对应的成就，收集10个以后算基本完成，将会出现这个区域特定的宝珠。收集25个以后，这个区域的宝珠会出现在别的区域。

基本的通关要求是，在9个区域里各收集10个收集品，然后在随之解锁的Hell里收集10个收集品，最后获取一个Hell特有的宝珠。但是，这个宝珠需要在触发之后，在距离100格的位置获取钥匙，再拿钥匙回来打开，这样才可以真正通关。值得一提的是，钥匙有指南针指示，但是回程是没有任何指示的。而和自己距离100格的格子有大约2×10^24个，因此不提前准备几乎一定会迷路。

那么，为了通关，还需要收集足够多的东西作为路标。墓地区域的宝珠“没有任何作用”，且可以随意丢弃。因此，方法就是收集足够多的墓地宝珠，沿路摆放，最终通关。


当然，我20个小时的体验里包括很慢的熟悉技巧，和各种各样的失败。大概总结一下通关技巧：

①既然墓地宝珠需要收集10个收集物，那么墓地自然也可以算作9个区域的选择之一；

②比较简单的区域是：初始冰地、塌方地面（速度快，不费事）、红蓝太阳（缺点是太慢）、扫雷（收集10个收集品之前基本没怪，推理的活）、镜子（收集品多，沿着十字路收集很快）、海滩（收集品多，在海滩能快速集齐）、藤蔓（每个藤蔓里都有收集品）、红绿开关（收集品多）、沙地（三角收集品多）；

③不要在猎狗区域收集，一会有用；

④击杀数目达到100才能解锁墓地，所以需要多打怪。

⑤当墓地区域收集10个后，快速离开，寻找十字路。这个时候十字路也会出现已完成区域的宝珠，包括墓地宝珠。否则一直在墓地不安全；

⑥主角的视野是7，所以至少要收集14个，不过建议应多尽多。在十字路耐心收集即可，并不危险；

⑦进入Hell区域后，建议先收集25个收集物，然后回到别的区域，最好是十字路。这个时候，通关宝珠将会在其它区域出现；

⑧最后找到猎狗区域。在这个区域耐心寻找，找到通关宝珠，然后一边扔路标一边找钥匙。选择这个区域的原因是，除非拿收集品，否则猎狗区域的猎狗不会主动攻击，非常安全；

⑨但是，拿到钥匙的一步会招来猎狗，所以最好提前准备一个分身或别的宝物。解决掉这波猎狗后，沿着路标回到宝珠即可通关。全程都不要收集宝物招惹猎狗。




以上就是我基于目前的体验，总结的所有内容了。

I'm not even gonna talk about the game other than say it's good, because other reviews can cover that. I'm going to talk about the absurdly powerful geometry sandbox that is included with the game.

You are probably aware that this game engine supports 2D hyperbolic space, but did you know it supports many types of 2D spherical spaces? And Euclidean spaces? And 3D hyperbolic, spherical, and Euclidean spaces? And even truly weird 3D spaces like Nil and Solv which make hyperbolic space feel like child's play. It's absurd how generalized the game mechanics have been programmed that the full game pretty much works just fine in different geometries, including 3D geometries. I mean, the developer could have optimized everything for a particular hyperbolic geometric tiling, but they put in a 3D engine and everything and let you play the game in first person (and other projections). Using the geometry browser, you can choose between dozens of different geometries to play on (and with modifiers like dual spaces, it probably extends to hundreds, and perhaps unlimited more using Archimedian notations and by loading geometries from files). While playing to win probably isn't fun or possible in many geometries, it's worth buying this game just to play around and visualize different geometries. Did I mention you can play a (simple) shoot-em up game in the different geometries?

The game even includes a aperiodic hat tiling, which was only recently discovered (in March 2023, I think). Humans didn't know if an aperiodic monotile existed before. That's right, the mad lad updated the game to include math we didn't even know existed before this year.

I can recommend this game to people who like games. But I can also recommend this game to people who don't like games but like math.

HyperRogue is a creative and unique game that I would recommend to anyone intrigued by the idea of a roguelike in a non-euclidean world. The gameplay is deceptively simple, as you just click the tiles around your character to move and interact with the world (or click yourself to pass the turn). However, there's a lot to this game despite how simple the controls are. Each area in the world has its own challenges, creatures, and style of non-euclidean geometry to navigate, The game does a good job of making these areas feel unique, and learning how to survive in each of them long enough to grab however many treasures you want and then leave is part of the fun. Speaking of treasures, how many collect in an area before trying to find a way to another area matters. Do you collect 10, enough to cause that area's unique powerup orbs to appear within that area? Or 25, causing that orb to have a chance to spawn in other areas, but making it much harder to escape as the difficulty is increased in that area with each treasure taken? Play This Game!!!!!
